note: The ordinary upload. Nothing is durable until the object exists and the API has re-read authorization.
Killed between two chunks. The staging file's synced length is the truth; HEAD reports it and the client resumes there.
Killed during verification. The session is still verifying, not durable; verification runs again from the whole file.

Killed between the rename and the report. The object exists named by a live upload row; startup reconciliation finishes the same transaction. This is the case that must never leave a mapping without bytes.
The API is down when the worker reports. Bytes are already safe; only durability waits. The worker retries and the report is idempotent.
The API is down mid-upload. PATCH needs no API, so bytes keep arriving; the upload stalls only when it needs a new capability.
Cloud is turned off mid-upload. The admitted chunk may finish; finalization is refused and nothing becomes durable.
Two devices race on the same picture. Allocation is idempotent by (workspace, incarnation, hash), so they converge on one session and one locator.
Corrupt bytes. Verification fails, the staging file is quarantined, and no mapping is written. A clean retry starts a new session.
The download. Association is written last, so a successful metadata lookup can never point at a partial file.
A download whose bytes do not hash. Quarantined, never rendered, never associated.
A session that expires without progress is reclaimed; one that keeps progressing is not.
